copy.blurb:
The model fancies Argentina more than the market does in this FIFA World Cup 2026 fixture against Jordan. +4.9pp is a narrow gap; that's what fires this as a Pick on the away side.

The Elo prior reads Jordan 1530 vs Argentina 2140: 610 points in favour of Argentina, which is a meaningful but not decisive prior. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Jordan to win at 3%, the draw at 10%, and Argentina to win at 87%. The Desk's three-way distribution is calibrated against the W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on, not against the exact scoreline. Argentina sits at 87% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Jordan to win at 6%, the draw at 12%, and Argentina to win at 82%. Polymarket has Argentina at 82%, which prices out at American odds of −471; the model has the same side at 87%. The +4.9pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Argentina the lower bound is 86%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +3.8pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. The Desk's posture is that calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures — we're not claiming the market is generally wrong, only that this side, on this fixture, looks mispriced. Selection is the dimension this verdict adds value on.

News will move the prior. With kickoff roughly 37 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. On a Pick this wide, it would take material news — a missing star, a tournament dropout, a venue change — to collapse the gap below the +3pp threshold; on the narrower side of the field, a single refresh can flip Pick to Pass. Either way, the Desk re-publishes after each refresh and does not recommend a trade.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Argentina a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +4.9pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
